narrative: OMX30 faces a compressed risk/reward this morning despite US market strength. Continental European weakness (DAX, CAC) correlates highly with Swedish equities and will likely dominate the open over transatlantic divergence. Technically, the index is deeply oversold (Stochastic K=10.6, RSI 39.34) and trading below its lower Bollinger Band, signaling potential mean reversion bounce, but ADX=22.5 with bearish DI tone and price -2.7% below the 50-MA (3180) suggest the primary trend remains pressured. US 10Y yield spike to 5.146% is a double-edged sword: positive for banks but negative DCF drag on tech/growth names. The negative correlation signal (-0.700%) and elevated VIX (+9.77%) amplify downside tail risk, particularly if Jobless Claims data disappoints at 14:30 CET.
morningBrief: OMX30 expected to open 0.3–0.6% lower, tracking Continental weakness and global risk-off sentiment. Key support: 3085 (lower Bollinger Band), critical support 3050. Resistance: 3123 (yesterday close), then 3180 (50-MA). Oversold conditions (Stochastic K=10.6, RSI 39.34) suggest potential for technical bounce intraday, but ADX=22.5 with bearish bias and price -2.7% below 50-MA indicate trend remains down. Sector rotation: Banks moderately positive on higher yields (NIM expansion); Industrials (Atlas Copco, Volvo) and Tech (Ericsson, Hexagon) under pressure from yield spike and NASDAQ disconnect. Volvo B watch for USD/SEK strength (+0.04%) offsetting industrial headwinds. Watch for mean reversion into oversold territory, but conviction remains low until 50-MA reclaimed. US Jobless Claims at 14:30 CET critical catalyst.
